summary: Find the credentials you are leaking, and the ones git remembers even after you deleted them.
highlights: Sixteen provider signatures, from Stripe and AWS to Supabase service_role keys
Reads git history, so an env file you deleted last month is still reported
Never prints a secret in full - the report does not become another copy of the key
Stays quiet about keys in a properly ignored .env, because that is where they belong
requires: python3 (already on macOS and Linux). Reads your project files and runs git log. No network.
notes: Finds what is on disk and in git history. It cannot tell you whether a leaked key has already been used - that needs the provider's logs - and it cannot see secrets already set in a deployed environment.
